nodes.name: Real function
nodes.description: A rule assigning to each x in the domain exactly one real value f(x).
nodes.source: PLACEHOLDER - Analisi I slides, intro to functions

nodes.name: Domain and neighbourhoods
nodes.description: The set where f is defined; a neighbourhood of x0 is an open interval around x0. Limits are taken at accumulation points of the domain.

nodes.name: Limit (intuitive idea)
nodes.description: f(x) gets arbitrarily close to L as x approaches x0, regardless of the value f(x0).

nodes.name: Limit (epsilon-delta definition)
nodes.description: For every epsilon > 0 there is delta > 0 such that 0 < |x - x0| < delta implies |f(x) - L| < epsilon.

nodes.name: One-sided limits
nodes.description: Limits as x approaches x0 from the left or the right; the limit exists iff both exist and are equal.

nodes.name: Limits at infinity and infinite limits
nodes.description: Behaviour of f(x) as x goes to plus or minus infinity, and limits whose value is infinite.

nodes.name: Algebra of limits
nodes.description: Limits of sums, products and quotients equal the sum, product and quotient of limits, when these are not indeterminate.

nodes.name: Indeterminate forms
nodes.description: Forms like 0/0, inf/inf, inf - inf, 0*inf, 1^inf, 0^0, inf^0 where the algebra of limits gives no answer; the limit can be any value or not exist.

nodes.name: Notable limits
nodes.description: Standard limits such as sin(x)/x -> 1, (1 + 1/x)^x -> e, (e^x - 1)/x -> 1, log(1+x)/x -> 1 as x -> 0 or infinity.

nodes.name: Continuity
nodes.description: f is continuous at x0 if the limit of f as x -> x0 exists and equals f(x0).

nodes.name: Types of discontinuity
nodes.description: Removable, jump and essential (second kind) discontinuities, classified by one-sided limits.

nodes.name: Little-o and asymptotic equivalence
nodes.description: f = o(g) if f/g -> 0; f ~ g if f/g -> 1. Used to simplify limits by replacing functions with equivalent ones.

nodes.name: Derivative
nodes.description: The limit of the difference quotient (f(x0+h) - f(x0))/h as h -> 0, when it exists.

nodes.name: L'Hopital's rule
nodes.description: For 0/0 or inf/inf forms, if f'/g' has a limit, f/g has the same limit (under the theorem's hypotheses).

nodes.name: Taylor expansion (Peano remainder)
nodes.description: Approximating f near x0 by a polynomial plus o((x - x0)^n); the standard tool for hard indeterminate forms.
